title: urnetwork / providers
description: The supply side of the network and the contracts it carries: the provider and extender populations with their ip family splits, the contract and dispute counts open now and over the trailing 24 hours, the countries with the most of each, and the egress buckets with the providers each egress rule leaves out and the backfill that answers for them. Internal: the contract counts are not published. Every gauge is replicated by every taskworker and read with max, so no panel needs a block or host variable; the one histogram, the backfill, is observed by each api process for its own answers and read as a rate summed across them. The ARIN database canary row reads the published canary decision, replicated by every taskworker like the other gauges, and each process's own ARIN slots.

panels.title: online providers
panels.description: Connected valid providers holding a public provide key. Every taskworker publishes the same measurement, so max selects it without replica skew.

panels.title: online providers
panels.description: The connected valid public provider population over time, refreshed on the collector's five minute database tick.

panels.title: online extenders

panels.title: online extenders
panels.description: The online extender population over time. An extender leaves it when its last address runs out of probe attempts, which is also what revokes its record.

panels.title: providers ipv4

panels.title: providers ipv6

panels.title: providers dualstack

panels.title: extenders ipv4

panels.title: extenders ipv6

panels.title: extenders dualstack

panels.title: providers by ip family

panels.title: share of open contracts with an extender party

targets.expr: max((max by (env,host,block,instance) (urnetwork_stats_open_contracts_with_extender{env="$env"}) and on (env,host,block,instance) (max by (env,host,block,instance) (urnetwork_stats_contract_open_status{env="$env",kind="with_extender",status="exact"}) == 1) and on (env,host,block,instance) ((time() - max by (env,host,block,instance) (urnetwork_stats_contract_open_observed_at_seconds{env="$env",kind="with_extender"})) < 600) and on (env,host,block,instance) ((time() - max by (env,host,block,instance) (urnetwork_stats_contract_open_observed_at_seconds{env="$env",kind="with_extender"})) >= -30)) / (max by (env,host,block,instance) (urnetwork_stats_open_contracts{env="$env"}) and on (env,host,block,instance) (max by (env,host,block,instance) (urnetwork_stats_contract_open_status{env="$env",kind="open",status="exact"}) == 1) and on (env,host,block,instance) ((time() - max by (env,host,block,instance) (urnetwork_stats_contract_open_observed_at_seconds{env="$env",kind="open"})) < 600) and on (env,host,block,instance) ((time() - max by (env,host,block,instance) (urnetwork_stats_contract_open_observed_at_seconds{env="$env",kind="open"})) >= -30)))

panels.description: Exact extender share from one complete PostgreSQL snapshot per process, then max across replicas. Same-process exact status and snapshot freshness within ten minutes are mandatory for both counts. Capped, unavailable, stale and old-schema counts produce no share; zero divided by zero is not a healthy zero. This stat queries only the current instant, never a historical last-not-null value.

panels.title: 24 hour dispute rate
panels.description: Disputed contracts as a fraction of the contracts created in the same trailing 24 hour window. Both numbers come from the same hour buckets, so a contract counted in one is counted in the other.

panels.title: top provider countries
panels.description: The ten countries with the most connected valid public providers. A country that loses its last provider has its series deleted on the next refresh, so it goes stale rather than pushing a stale count forever.

panels.title: top extender countries
panels.description: The ten countries with the most online extenders, by the country each extender last activated from. An extender whose activation resolved no country is counted in the population total and has no series here.

panels.title: egress buckets
panels.description: The three buckets FindProviders2 answers from and the providers each egress rule leaves out (connect/GEOMAP.md §10). Membership here is the rules' alone -- the hard exclusions, the country gate and the 90 % rule -- before the reliability and performance minimums of the score cache, over the connected valid public providers the online gauge counts.

panels.title: quality bucket
panels.description: Probed providers past the hard exclusions and the country gate whose latest health run passed at least nine in ten of its real-site loads. The default rank mode draws from these.

panels.title: speed bucket
panels.description: Every probed provider past the hard exclusions and the country gate, whatever its run found, ordered by latency and throughput alone.

panels.title: online bucket
panels.description: Providers with no probe verdict -- none within the evidence age, or a run of too few loads -- past the exclusions and the country gate. The score cache admits those that pass the reliability floors and the speed-mode score maximum, so a provider no client has measured is not admitted. No request names this bucket; a short quality or speed answer borrows from it last, ordered by reliability. It grows when the probe pipeline stops or covers little of the fleet.

panels.title: quality bucket at index 0
panels.description: Quality providers whose latest run had no failed load at all -- the only ones that can carry tier 0, which the client requires before a network's own provider carries a fresh web session.

panels.title: quality share of online providers
panels.description: The quality bucket as a fraction of the connected valid public providers, both counted by the same collector tick over the same population. Near zero while the probe samples fewer loads than a run needs to be evidence, when the online bucket answers instead.

panels.title: left out: blackhole
panels.description: Providers with a current blackhole verdict: absent from every bucket, every count, force_minimum and an explicit client id. The verdict lifts by itself when the next check passes. A wave here is the checker before it is the fleet (GEOMAP §11.2).

panels.title: left out: tls
panels.description: Providers whose latest health run saw a TLS-authentication failure: a forged identity on one destination, absent everywhere like a blackhole until a later run is clean.

panels.title: left out: country
panels.description: Providers a fresh probe observed exiting in a country other than the one they are listed in: out of every bucket and the counts as a minimum, still reachable with force_minimum or an explicit client id. Only a derived location that crossed a border can put a provider here, and the derive job refuses those, so anything above zero is worth a look.

panels.title: left out: no url success
panels.description: Providers measured at least twice in the last eight hours without one URL success, in a country where the probe works: out of every bucket and the counts, Online included, until their first success. Not a hard exclusion: probes, force_minimum and an explicit client id still reach them. A country where fewer than online_success_country_floor of the measured providers have a success is exempt (see the exempt countries panel), unless online_url_success_ratio is on with online_url_ratio_country_exemption: false, which takes them out there too; online_requires_url_success: false in provider.yml turns the rule off.

panels.title: left out: low url ratio
panels.description: Providers measured at least twice in the last eight hours with a URL success but a share of successes below online_url_success_ratio: out of every bucket and the counts, Online included, until their share reaches the ratio. Zero while online_url_success_ratio is 0, the default (off). Not a hard exclusion: probes, force_minimum and an explicit client id still reach them. A country the URL-success rule exempts keeps them unless online_url_ratio_country_exemption is false; online_requires_url_success: false turns the ratio off with the rule.

panels.title: out of quality and speed: health
panels.description: Probed providers that failed more than one in five of their real-site loads: out of quality and speed, still in the online bucket and the counts.

panels.title: out of quality or speed: unprobed or warming up
panels.description: Providers with no native verdict yet, all in the online bucket and counted. Unprobed: no probe evidence within the evidence age, out of quality and speed. Warming up: URL checks that pass, on too few runs for the native minimums (quality needs 3 runs spanning 30 minutes, speed 2): out of quality, and out of speed below 2 runs. A new provider's paced runs meet both about 40 minutes after its first. A wave that drains within the hour is new providers warming up; one that holds is the prober or its capacity. Neither is a quality problem.

panels.title: left out in total
panels.description: Every provider left out of at least one bucket, each counted once under the first rule that holds, in the order reliability, arin_risk, tls, no_success, low_success, then unprobed with no evidence or health, then not_modern, then unprobed while warming up (passing URL checks on too few runs), then arin_non_quality. Blackhole and country are legacy labels that stay zero.

panels.title: providers left out, by reason
panels.description: The providers each rule leaves out over time. Reliability, arin_risk and tls remove a provider from everything; no_success and low_success (only while online_url_success_ratio is on) from every bucket and the counts while their probes continue; health, unprobed with no evidence and not_modern (only while the modern provider gate is on) from quality and speed; unprobed while warming up (passing URL checks on too few runs) from quality, and from speed below 2 runs; arin_non_quality from quality alone. Every reason is published every refresh, zero included.

panels.title: borrowed providers, by rank mode
panels.description: Providers per second that FindProviders2 answers borrowed from outside the requested bucket -- the other bucket, then the probed past their cutoffs, then online -- summed over every api process. A mass probe failure shows here as a wave of backfill beside the reasons it follows from.

panels.title: borrowed per answer, by rank mode
panels.description: The mean number of borrowed providers in a non-forced answer to a location request. Zero is every answer filled from its own bucket; the request count is the ceiling.

panels.title: providers per bucket
panels.description: The three buckets over time. Quality is a subset of speed; online is disjoint from both. A fall in quality and speed with online rising is a probe outage the online bucket is answering for.

panels.title: quality bucket by egress index
panels.description: The quality bucket stacked by egress index: the weighted real-site loads of the latest run that failed every retry, capped. "none" is a row the new rollup has not written, ranked on the net-type score. The index sets the quality tier.

panels.title: speed bucket by egress index
panels.description: The speed bucket stacked by the same index. Speed ranks on latency and throughput alone, so the index does not order it; the split shows how much of the probed supply quality would admit.

panels.title: quality bucket by egress index, now
panels.description: The current distribution of the quality bucket over the index, every index up to the settings' largest published, zero included.

panels.title: share of answers backfilled, by rank mode
panels.description: The fraction of non-forced location answers that borrowed at least one provider. Speed answers borrow in most locations while few providers pass the speed cutoffs; a rise in quality answers is a bucket emptying.

panels.title: answers by result count, by rank mode
panels.description: Non-forced FindProviders2 answers per second by how many providers they held, after every request-time filter, summed over every api process. The backfill exists to keep the 0 and 1-2 bands empty; answers there while the buckets above are empty are a probe outage the online bucket could not cover.

panels.title: borrowed share of answered providers, by rank mode
panels.description: Of every provider non-forced location answers handed out, the share borrowed from outside the requested bucket. Backfill makes every answer look full, so this is the operator's view of how empty the bucket behind it is; above half for an hour is the backfill-sustained finding of SIGNALS.md §2.19b.

panels.title: online fallback lent, by evidence
panels.description: Providers per second that the Online fallback lent Quality and Speed answers, by what the draw knew of them: url_reliability (URL-probe evidence and a reliability score), url (URL-probe evidence only), reliability (a reliability score only) or none. Summed over every process that answers FindProviders2 (the api, and the proxy for its hosted devices), whether or not egress_index.rank_measured_first orders the draw by it. The none share is the unchecked supply those answers carry; with the setting on, it falls to what the measured providers cannot fill.

panels.title: online url-success rule: exempt countries
panels.description: The countries the URL-success rule exempts because fewer than online_success_country_floor of their measured Online providers have a URL success in eight hours: the probe itself fails there for most providers, so their providers keep the benefit of the doubt. Each bar is the providers without a success the exemption keeps online, and while online_url_success_ratio is on those below it too, from the guard the last score export published; zero with online_url_ratio_country_exemption: false, which applies the ratio in every country. No bars while the rule is disabled.

panels.title: online url-success rule: kept by exempt countries
panels.description: The providers without a URL success, and while online_url_success_ratio is on those below it, the rule keeps online because their country is exempt, over time; the providers it excludes are the no_success and low_success reasons beside the backfill. A country entering the exempt set is a probe failing there, not its providers; raise online_success_country_floor to exempt more countries, or set online_requires_url_success: false in provider.yml to turn the rule off.

panels.title: out of quality and speed: not modern
panels.description: Providers the modern provider gate takes out of quality and speed: the URL probe has not shown end-to-end post-quantum encryption with resizable transfer windows on their sessions in the last seven days. They stay online and counted, and probes, force_minimum and an explicit client id still reach them. Zero until the gate turns on by itself at 2026-10-21 00:00 UTC while quality_speed_requires_modern_provider is absent from provider.yml (or at quality_speed_modern_provider_start), and while the switch is false; the shadow beside it says what the gate would take out.

panels.title: modern gate shadow: quality not modern
panels.description: Of the providers the other rules admit to quality, those the modern provider gate would take out: no probe evidence, evidence older than seven days, or a latest observation without post-quantum encryption or without resizable windows. The same whether the gate is on or off; review it before the gate turns on by itself at 2026-10-21 00:00 UTC, and postpone with quality_speed_requires_modern_provider: false, a config release and a taskworker and API restart, if it would gut the bucket (the monitor warns from 72 hours before, SIGNALS.md §2.29).

panels.title: modern gate shadow: speed not modern
panels.description: Of the providers the other rules admit to speed, those the modern provider gate would take out, for the same reasons as quality. The same whether the gate is on or off.

panels.title: modern gate shadow: modern share of quality
panels.description: The share of the providers the other rules admit to quality that the probe has shown to be modern, which is the share of quality the gate would keep. Rises as probes that report the evidence measure the fleet; no value while quality is empty.

panels.title: modern gate: on
panels.description: Whether the modern provider gate holds quality and speed to modern providers under the taskworkers' own provider.yml, as their stats collector last read it: on from the scheduled start while quality_speed_requires_modern_provider is absent, never with it false, at once with it true. The largest of the taskworkers, so a config rollout reads on as soon as one has flipped.

panels.title: modern gate: scheduled start
panels.description: The instant the modern provider gate turns on by itself, 2026-10-21 00:00 UTC unless quality_speed_modern_provider_start moves it. No value while provider.yml sets quality_speed_requires_modern_provider, true or false, when no flip is scheduled. The monitor's readiness signal (SIGNALS.md §2.29) watches the shadow from 72 hours before it.

panels.title: rank measured first: on

targets.expr: min by (service) ((max by (service, host, instance) (urnetwork_findproviders2_rank_measured_first_enabled{env="$env",service=~"api|proxy"}) and on (service, host, instance) max by (service, host, instance) (process_start_time_seconds{env="$env",service=~"api|proxy"})) or on (service, host, instance) (0 * max by (service, host, instance) (process_start_time_seconds{env="$env",service=~"api|proxy"})))

panels.description: Whether the api and the proxy order their FindProviders2 draws by evidence (egress_index.rank_measured_first in provider.yml), as each process read it. "every process" compares the gauge with the independent process_start_time_seconds inventory by service, host and instance: a process without the gauge counts as off, including an old binary. It is on only once every inventoried process applies the setting, and has no value when no process inventory is visible. During a staggered restart, drained processes can keep it off until their series become stale; "any process" is on as soon as one publishes on. Turning it on or off is a config release and a restart of the api and the proxy; the taskworker needs nothing.

panels.title: modern gate shadow: quality by outcome
panels.description: The providers the other rules admit to quality, by what the modern provider gate decides for them: modern (kept), not_post_quantum and no_resizable_windows (measured without the capability), no_evidence (never measured with the evidence) and stale_evidence (last measured over seven days ago). no_evidence falls as probes report the evidence; a rise in not_post_quantum or no_resizable_windows is providers on older or custom builds.

panels.title: modern gate shadow: speed by outcome
panels.description: The providers the other rules admit to speed, by what the modern provider gate decides for them, with the outcomes of the quality panel beside it.

panels.title: egress site pool and dark verdicts
panels.description: The prober's dark verdicts and the destination pool its health runs load (the geomap design, §11.3 and §11.4). The fleet shares are snapshots each taskworker takes for itself, so they are read from the one with the freshest snapshot; the pool gauges are read from the taskworker that ran the latest refresh; the prober's and the refresh's event counters are summed across the taskworkers on the egress probes dashboard.

panels.title: fleet dark share

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_dark_share{env="$env"} and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, (max by (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"}) > time() - 900) and (max by (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"}) <= time() + 30)))

panels.description: The share of the providers with a current measured blackhole check that are dark. Dark is a verdict over consecutive failed checks -- three in a row spanning at least 30 minutes by default (geomap §11.3) -- never a single failed check, and one passing check clears it; only a tls authentication failure is dark at once. Read from the one taskworker with the freshest fleet snapshot.

panels.title: fleet failure share by class

targets.expr: max by (class) (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_failure_share{env="$env"} and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, (max by (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"}) > time() - 900) and (max by (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"}) <= time() + 30)))

panels.description: The failed share of the scored loads, after retries, of the health runs measured within the prober-fault window (an hour by default), per class and over all of them. Above the 20 % prober-fault line across every class for an hour is a fault on the prober -- its request shape or its capacity -- not on the sites (monitor signal §2.19b), and the pool refresh skips its run while the share of the loads that reached their provider is over the line, or while fewer than a fifth of the recent loads reached their provider at all (this panel counts every failure, a provider that was never reached included). Read from the one taskworker with the freshest fleet snapshot.

panels.title: batch guard share
panels.description: The share the batch guard judged in the latest batch of each schedule: for blackhole, dark checks over measured checks, against its 0.2 guard line; for full, failed scored loads over scored loads, against its 0.3 guard line. Each taskworker keeps the share of its own latest batch until it runs another, so this is the highest of those shares; a value over its line is a batch the guard held. The trips are counted on the egress probes dashboard.

panels.title: site pool refresh, last run
panels.description: Time since a taskworker last completed the daily pool refresh, refreshed or skipped, so this saw-tooths between zero and a day. Amber past 25 h, a run is late; red past two days, the refresh is not running (monitor signal §2.19b refresh not running): its task is missing, parked or failing. The time is kept by the process that ran the refresh, so right after every taskworker restarts this reads as decades until the next daily run.

panels.title: site failure share (worst 15)

targets.expr: topk(15, max by (site, class) (urnetwork_egress_site_failure_share{env="$env"} and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, max by (env,service,block,host,instance) (urnetwork_egress_site_refresh_last_run_timestamp_seconds{env="$env"}))))

panels.description: The latest refresh's failure share of each active site: the share of the runs on healthy exits, those that passed nine in ten of the other sites, in which the site failed every attempt (over every exit the probe reached when too few qualified; a run that never reached its provider is in no site's share). Read from the taskworker that ran the latest refresh; a skipped refresh judges nothing, so after one this shows that taskworker's last judged shares, or none. A site over the 50 % retire line across at least 200 judged runs is retired by the next refresh, at most one per class per run; one that stays over it for a day is the pool-needs-refresh finding of monitor signal §2.19b.

panels.title: site pool by class

targets.expr: max by (class, state) (urnetwork_egress_site_pool_size{env="$env"} and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, max by (env,service,block,host,instance) (urnetwork_egress_site_refresh_last_run_timestamp_seconds{env="$env"})))

panels.description: Destination pool rows per class after the latest refresh, by state: scored sites count toward the index and the 90 % rule, probation sites are loaded and recorded but not yet counted, and candidates are promotable now. Read from the taskworker that ran the latest refresh. An active pool under the class's pool size, or no candidates left to promote, is the pool-thin finding of monitor signal §2.19b.

panels.title: canary state
panels.description: The state the latest score publication's ARIN canary decision ended in (arindbctl/ARINDB.md, Dual-database canary): single when the indexer has no usable old database, warming while too few providers carry facts for both databases, latest when the comparison passes, fallback when the latest tripped the breaker and the export serves the old database's Quality classification. Risk always comes from the latest database. Read from the published decision by every taskworker; nothing shows while no decision is readable, when readers serve each provider's latest slot.

panels.title: fallback active
panels.description: 1 while the score export serves the old ARIN database's Quality classification because the latest tripped the breaker: a bucket's net loss above bucket_loss_threshold or a country with no supply left in a bucket. Pages (ArinDbFallbackActive). A fallback restores Quality only; a Speed or Online loss comes from risk, which always follows the latest database and pages separately.

panels.title: serving database
panels.description: Build time of the ARIN database whose Quality classification the score export and every request-time reader serve. The epoch 0 (shown as 1970) means each provider's latest slot, as before the canary: the single state, or no readable decision.

panels.title: decision age
panels.description: Time since the indexer last published a canary decision; every score publication publishes one before its export. Over 30 minutes is ArinDbDecisionStale: the indexer is stalled, and its decision expires with the publication's 300 minute ttl, after which readers serve each provider's latest slot.

panels.title: bucket supply under each database
panels.description: Public providers with facts for both ARIN databases in each bucket under the latest and under the old database, counted by the export's unchanged rules with only the ARIN facts substituted. Risk removes a provider from every bucket and non-quality only from Quality, so Speed and Online differ between the databases only through risk.

panels.title: net loss of latest against old
panels.description: (old - latest) / old supply per bucket over the paired providers; negative is a gain and 0 means no old supply. The breaker trips when a bucket is strictly above bucket_loss_threshold (0.10 by default, the line). A Speed or Online loss above it pages (ArinDbRiskSupplyLoss) without an automatic repair, because only risk causes it and risk always follows the latest database.

panels.title: coverage of the public cohort
panels.description: Share of the public score cohort whose rollup carries facts for the latest database, the old database, or both (paired). Below min_coverage (0.98 by default, the line) the run is warming and serves the database the rows carry: processes not yet restarted onto the pair, a rollup not yet refreshed after a release, or a stuck host. Warming for two hours warns (ArinDbCanaryWarming).

panels.title: emptied countries and cities
panels.description: Countries and cities with supply in a bucket under the old ARIN database and none under the latest. An emptied country trips the breaker when trip_on_emptied_country is set (the default); emptied cities are reported only, and their names are in the published decision and the indexer log.

panels.title: countries the latest would empty
panels.description: Each country the latest database would empty, per bucket, with the old database's supply there. Monitor signal §2.9d names these countries in its page.

panels.title: supply by country under each database
panels.description: Paired public providers per bucket and published country under each database. Providers without a published country count only in the bucket totals.

panels.title: the indexer's pair
panels.description: The latest and old databases the score export compared, from its own loader: build epoch, state and the SHA-256 their manifests record. The old database is the byte copy arindbctl update made of the previously selected release (arin-old.mmdb); a refused copy ships the release without one, and the state is then missing.

panels.title: each process's slots

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_arin_database_info{env="$env"}) by (service, host, block, instance, slot, state, sha256)

panels.description: Both ARIN slots of every process that opened a pair, pushed with the process's own labels: loaded, missing, identical, invalid or unopened, with the manifest hash (none when unknown). Connect, API, MCP and Alt open the pair at warmup; Taskworker at its first score publication. A process keeps its pair until it restarts.

panels.title: each process's database ages

targets.expr: time() - max by (service, host, block, instance) (urnetwork_arin_database_build_epoch_seconds{env="$env"} > 0)
time() - max by (service, host, block, instance) (urnetwork_arin_old_database_build_epoch_seconds{env="$env"} > 0)

panels.description: Time since the build of each process's latest and old ARIN databases; a slot that is not loaded is left out. Processes at different latest ages are a fleet not yet restarted onto a release, which keeps the canary warming.

panels.title: decision conditions
panels.description: The conditions of the latest decision, 1 while each holds (arindbctl/ARINDB.md, Dual-database canary). warming_tripped: warming's paired sample trips, so the latest is not served (page). warming_serves_latest: warming serves the latest unverified. latched: a fallback holds until release_passing_runs comparisons pass with release_margin. accepted: provider.yml accept_latest_build_epoch names the latest. latest_unavailable: the publishing Taskworker could not open its latest (page). pair_carried: the pair compared is the previous decision's. fallback_dropped: single right after a fallback (page).

panels.title: net gain of latest against old
panels.description: The latest database's net gain of paired supply in each bucket, (latest - old) / old. The breaker trips only on losses; a gain above 0.10 with at least 20 paired providers of old supply pages as a possible flood, which the fallback cannot judge.

panels.title: gross churn of latest against old
panels.description: The latest database's gross churn of paired supply in each bucket, (removed + added) / old. The net loss hides a release that moves as many providers out of a bucket as into it; churn above 0.20 with at least 20 paired providers of old supply pages.

panels.title: public cohort against its recent size
panels.description: The public providers the canary compared, and the largest cohort of the last two hours. A provider whose latest lookup fails never writes a location, so it never reaches the cohort and the comparison cannot see it; a release whose records fail to decode shows as a shrinking cohort and as ARIN lookup errors on the services overview.

panels.title: cohort loss against its recent size
panels.description: The cohort's loss against its largest size over the last two hours. Above 0.10, from a reference of at least 100 providers, it pages: providers are leaving the cohort before the canary can compare them.

panels.title: serving changes and latch release
panels.description: Changes of the serving epoch over the last six hours, which page above 4 as a canary switching the fleet back and forth, and the consecutive comparisons a latched fallback has passed with the release margin; it releases at release_passing_runs (default 6).

panels.title: decision reads that were not ok
panels.description: The share of every process's reads of the published decision that were absent or expired, invalid, or a Redis error. Absent and invalid decisions serve each provider's latest slot; an error keeps the process's last decision for up to 15 minutes. Above 0.05 for 15 minutes it warns.

panels.title: compared pair's age
panels.description: Time since the canary first compared its current pair of databases. The cohort-shrink page fires only within two hours of a new pair, or while latest lookups fail, so a Connect outage or a restart is not blamed on a release.
